chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, from some of his men and Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya all together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Amara Hamza ibn at-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If two men remained on the earth, one of them would be the Hujjah (proof/authority) over the other.

key_terms.الْأَرْض: The earth, representing the realm of human existence.
key_terms.حُجَّة: Hujjah (Proof/Authority), referring to the Imam who serves as the definitive proof of God on earth.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Hujjah in Shia theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq emphasizes the indispensability of the *Hujjah* (Proof of God) as the sole source of divine authority, even in a hypothetical scenario of minimal humanity. It reinforces the Shia doctrine that the Imam is not merely a political leader but the essential metaphysical link between God and creation, ensuring the continuity of guidance regardless of population size. This concept aligns with the principle of *Ijma'* (consensus) on the Imamate, where the presence of the Imam validates the religious and intellectual orientation of the world.
